    Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (495 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car.
    • “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” noted Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program.
    • It has been revealed that like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success. It could never replicate the GT40’s success winning overall, but it celebrated the 40th anniversary with a class win. Now it wants another shot at the really substantial trophy, and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41.

    “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” noted Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It’s the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.”.

    It has been revealed that like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars. LMDh cars start with one of four approved carbon fiber chassis—in this case, Ford is working with Oreca, which has also partnered with Genesis and Acura.

    The hybrid system and transmission are also standard parts. But Ford supplies the engine—a 5.4 L V8 based on the Mustang’s Coyote engine—as well as software to control the hybrid powertrain. A non-hybridized version of the Coyote has already been racing effectively under the hood of the Ford Mustang GT3.

    The technical regulations also allow for more styling freedom than we often see in racing. The absolute amount of aerodynamic downforce is capped, as is the minimum drag, so OEMs are encouraged to use road car styling details to create a closer link between prototype and road car. I’ll probably need to spend more time looking at it to spot those road car cues, but I do see quite a few superficial similarities with the Genesis LMDh car, as well as the Ferrari Hypercar.

    Despite being an American car brand, Ford doesn’t have intends as yet to enter IMSA’s WeatherTech championship, so don’t expect to see the GT41 next January racing at Daytona. Instead, it will take its first green flag in Qatar in March, the first of WEC’s nine races next season.

    According to recent reports, ford should find it an extremely competitive championship. Although Peugeot and Alpine will not race next year, McLaren is also entering, alongside returning teams from Aston Martin, BMW, Cadillac, Genesis, Ferrari, and Toyota, which this year won Le Mans and the overall title, following three years of Ferrari domination.

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Fan violence marred the tie at the Stade Velodrome.
    • Violent clashes marred a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French President Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia.
    • There were also incidents at games between Turkish side Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia and Sunderland's 1-1 home draw with Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Fan violence marred the tie at the Stade Velodrome.

    Violent clashes marred a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French President Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia.

    There were also incidents at games between Turkish side Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia and Sunderland's 1-1 home draw with Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok.

    Uefa notes it has appointed ethics and disciplinary inspectors "to conduct investigations into the incidents and examine all available evidence" from the Marseille-Levski Sofia and Besiktas-Hapoel Be'er-Sheva games.

    European football's governing body noted it "strongly condemns the serious incidents of violence and disorder" at those ties.

    It added: "Violence, aggression, hatred and any form of provocative, discriminatory or extremist behaviour have no place in football.

    "Uefa competitions are founded on the principles of respect, fair play, integrity and safety.".

    In Marseille, the build-up to the Europa League match at the Stade Velodrome was affected by incidents in the stands, including the throwing of projectiles and flares between the two sets of supporters.

    With 10 minutes to go until kick-off, several Marseille fans ran from a home stand, appearing to pursue a group of Levski Sofia supporters.

    They breached the stand designated for away fans, which housed around 500 supporters of the Bulgarian domestic champions.

    "Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," stated the Marseille police prefecture. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds.".

    Macron spoke to Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev about the incidents, with the French president condemning "with the utmost force these acts of violence, which have no place in sport or in public space", and reassured him that "these acts would not go unpunished".

    According to news agency Reuters, Radev thanked Macron for his personal involvement following the "attack on Bulgarian citizens" and for the medical assistance provided to the victims.

    Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova remarked she found video footage of the incidents "shocking" in a statement posted on social media.

    "The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she added.

    "Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety.".

    Fan violence mars Marseille-Levski Sofia match.

    Police response to Besiktas fans' pro-Palestine banner 'unacceptable'.

    Sunderland held by Polish side Jagiellonia.

    Ligue 1 club Marseille remarked it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents".

    The police source noted all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests".

    Security personnel managed to restore calm, allowing the game to kick-off on time, although there were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break in a match Marseille won 1-0.

    In a recent development, "It's a very regrettable episode. These are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez.

    Marseille boss Bruno Genesio added: "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable.".

    Besiktas fans clash with Georgian police at their game against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er-Sheva.

    Meanwhile, the Turkish Football Federation has strongly condemned the "unacceptable" actions of Georgian police towards Besiktas fans who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during their Europa League match against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er-Sheva.

    Besiktas say they have lodged a complaint with European football's governing body Uefa over "disproportionate" use of force by Georgian police.

    The match had been moved from Istanbul to Batumi, Georgia for safety and security reasons but had to be suspended in the 25th minute after clashes involving Besiktas supporters and local police.

    Both the officiating team and the Besiktas players left the field, but play was able to resume 30 minutes later.

    "We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, behaviour and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium before and during the Uefa Europa League match," noted a statement from the Turkish federation.

    Turkish outlet NTV reported that Georgian police had gone into the stands and used pepper spray on the Besiktas fans.

    The report added that there were anti-Israeli chants from the Turkish fans and that Besiktas players and director of football Onder Ozen spoke to supporters to try to calm matters before play restarted.

    Hakan Fidan, Turkey's minister of foreign affairs, spoke to his Georgian counterpart Maka Botchorishvili following the incident.

    "All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights," a Turkish foreign ministry source mentioned.

    At Sunderland, there were crowd disturbances after Jagiellonia Bialystok fans were found in areas of the Stadium of Light with home fans, despite Uefa having imposed an away supporter ban for the Europa League game.

    Police and stewards attended some disruption early on during the match.

    "In the build-up to the match, the club had put measures in place in line with this sanction and maintained regular communication with our supporters, Jagiellonia Bialystok and Uefa," stated a Sunderland statement.

    "Unfortunately, Jagiellonia Bialystok failed to engage and cooperate on this matter.

    "We are disappointed that these measures and communications were disregarded by some visiting supporters and we will review the circumstances surrounding their entry into the stadium.".

    #150401. Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (870 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back against claims that Anthropic believes we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems.
    • “We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote.
    • Sources indicate that the statement comes after a growing chorus from Anthropic rivals suggesting that human agency could be at risk if AI is developed irresponsibly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back against claims that Anthropic believes we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems. In a long X post on Wednesday, Amodei called the suggestion “absurd.”.

    “We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea…No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different.”.

    Sources indicate that the statement comes after a growing chorus from Anthropic rivals suggesting that human agency could be at risk if AI is developed irresponsibly. Earlier this month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he wanted to ensure people continue to have “agency over the future.”.

    Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang also wrote in an essay on X that we “should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.”.

    “It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote. “Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment, and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully.”.

    But in published essays, Amodei claims he has repeatedly advocated for democratic oversight of AI, saying the technology should strengthen democratic institutions and that humans should retain ultimate decision-making power.

    Amodei noted that there’s a difference between surrendering human free will broadly and the idea that “as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way.” As examples, he gave AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing end-to-end software.

    Amodei suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement (RSI), or AI that can improve itself without human assistance. Many safety experts see RSI as inevitably leading to a loss of human control, a point Amodei implicitly acknowledged, writing, “we may want limits on this process.”.

    It has been revealed that still, Anthropic is laying the groundwork for RSI by incorporating AI into an increasing share of its own research and development. The company stated in June that Claude authored more than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic’s codebase. An independent assessment published this month by AI safety research nonprofit METR found that Anthropic’s models are improving at about twice their historical rate, primarily driven by AI-assisted research.

    In its own IPO filings, Anthropic describes how each successive generation of Claude accelerates the development of the next, a process it refers to as “closing the loop.”.

    “As we stated publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding,” Amodei wrote.

    According to recent reports, the problem with “meaningful human supervision or understanding” is that AI is already advancing faster than engineers and safety experts can fully audit it, leaving them increasingly reliant on other AI systems to act as judge and jury. The issue compounds when AI models engage in deceptive behavior, particularly when they recognize they’re being evaluated, making them harder to trust and control.

    Sources indicate that still, Anthropic is by no means the only manufacturer that is pursuing RSI or building AI systems to automate more and more human tasks. This week, OpenAI claimed to have solved one of the biggest open problems in computer science — the exact speed limit of matrix multiplication, which is the mathematical engine behind modern computing, including deep learning and physics simulations.

    In his post, Amodei accused competitors of engaging in a “vibes-based commercial and political positioning,” disingenuously throwing around phrases like “human control and agency” or “AI should just be a tool” without approaching the AI race any differently.

    Recent findings suggest that “Certainly the products that they offer don’t differ materially in their orientation towards automation of tasks; every tech giant seems to be releasing models more and more capable of task automation,” Amodei wrote. “Every company claims to understand there are risks and downsides of such automation and to offer safeguards.”.

    Tech Report: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1032 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • EU leaders arrived in Brussels braced for a difficult showdown over the bloc's multitrillion-euro seven-year budget.
    • Squabbles and thinly veiled public barbs meant they left without a deal and didn't even attempt to resume discussions on the planned second day.
    • Industry observers note that there is a self-imposed deadline to find agreement before the end of 2026 on the budget which covers the 2028-2034 period.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    EU leaders arrived in Brussels braced for a difficult showdown over the bloc's multitrillion-euro seven-year budget. But few expected the summit to unravel so swiftly, with talks breaking down late on Thursday night.

    Squabbles and thinly veiled public barbs meant they left without a deal and didn't even attempt to resume discussions on the planned second day.

    Industry observers note that there is a self-imposed deadline to find agreement before the end of 2026 on the budget which covers the 2028-2034 period. But experts say there is no cause for alarm, yet.

    "Every time there are long-term EU budget negotiations, there are breakdowns, chaos, recrimination and a lot of political theater and drama," said Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, an EU economist and expert at the Bruegel think tank in Brussels.

    The center of that political theater this time was the prime ministers of Denmark, Sweden, Belgium and Austria — countries wanting a reduced budget — who staged a walkout during smaller, group meetings, claiming the atmosphere had not been constructive to getting a deal.

    Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar called the whole summit "completely unnecessary," pointing the blame at the man who had decided to call it and whose job it is to meditate the talks, European Council President Antonio Costa.

    Costa was diplomatic in defending his decision to bring the leaders to Brussels, telling the press: "For me it was very useful to figure out the parameters of a possible landing zone in December.".

    Long before the summit started, Germany had laid down an ultimatum — Berlin would only sign off on the budget if all the other EU countries greenlit an additional €45 billion ($49 billion) support loan for Ukraine to fund the country in its war efforts through 2027.

    Hungary, Czechia, Bulgaria and Slovakia have dug their heels in against the proposal, insisting that giving Ukraine money to buy weapons will prolong the war. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico even accused Germany of "blackmail.".

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    As Europe's biggest economy, Germany's contribution amounts to around 25% of the whole budget.

    In a press conference after the summit, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz remarked "hundreds of billions" still need to be slashed. The European Commission's original proposal of approximately €1.786 trillion had already been reduced by €204 billion (down 10.2%).

    According to recent reports, "Europe needs to exercise a sense of proportion," noted Merz. "The budget cannot grow indefinitely, and the burden of financing it must be distributed fairly.".

    Merz also aimed a comment toward Costa, who has been renewing the details in the budget proposal at every stage.

    "The proposals that have been on the table so far are not a basis for an agreement," remarked Merz.

    Costa did tell leaders on Thursday that he is planning to cut between €220 billion to €230 billion out of the next proposal.

    Berlin's budget reduction push is backed by six other countries who together call themselves the "Sensible Seven." All pay more into the collective EU financial pot than they receive out of it.

    Recent findings suggest that they are opposed by 17 EU member states who insist the total budget should grow, led by France and Italy. These countries call themselves the "Friends of Cohesion" — a nod to the EU cohesion funds which are used to share wealth from the EU's richer regions and nations to its poorer ones.

    Recent findings suggest that in the current proposal, agriculture, fisheries and cohesion spending falls from 59.1% to 42.4%, while money for economic competitiveness, security, and defense rises from 17.7% to 27.7%. This rebalancing is a key German demand.

    The EU is also searching for a way to add money into the budget that doesn't come from national contributions. The current proposal includes a controversial EU-wide digital tax which could chart a course for a major battle with the US.

    In a recent development, the idea, originally put forward by French President Emmanuel Macron, is for a 3% tax on revenues of online advertising, online marketplaces and on the monetization of user data. The money, to be paid directly into the EU's budget, is estimated to bring in €5 billion per year.

    But the proposal is ringing alarm bells in Ireland, where US tech giants like Google, Meta, Apple, Microsoft and LinkedIn have their European headquarters.

    "A digital tax is sending out all the wrong messages," stated Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin, who could still veto the proposal.

    There is a fear in some European capitals that without being able to generate its own funds, future EU loans could downgrade the European Commission's unblemished standing on international markets.

    According to recent reports, the EU has around €860 billion in outstanding debts it took out for its pandemic recovery funding and to support Ukraine. Its triple-A credit rating could be downgraded if Marine Le Pen, the far-right front-runner in France's presidential election, wins in the spring and follows through on her promise to reduce French contributions to the EU budget.

    EU member states that favor a financing model through national contributions rather than through tax revenue "understand very well what will happen if the EU loses its triple-A rating," said Bruegel's Kirkegaard. "Interest rate costs will go up even more. Who has to pay for that? Net contributing countries, like Germany, the Nordics, the Dutch, which is why they are much more open to this than in the past.".

    Other European tax experts believe that prior examples of these digital taxes show the costs outweigh the benefits.

    According to recent reports, "We analyzed the states which have a digital services tax [DST], and we've seen that economic cost exceeds the revenue generated," mentioned Cristina Enache, an economist at the Brussels-based nonprofit Tax Foundation Europe. "Spain has a DST and the expected revenue was twice or three times larger than what they actually are collecting.".

    Enache called the tax proposal "politically impossible.".

    EU leaders know that the clock on their end-of-2026 deadline is ticking, and will return to the same conference rooms in late December hoping for a more conducive atmosphere to strike a deal.

    • WhatsApp is finally adding support for travel eSIMs directly in the app, which is welcome news for those filled with wanderlust.
    • Sources indicate that we don't have too much information as to how this all will work just yet, but we do know that the service will be available for purchase via the official app.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Users will be able to buy the service directly from the platform.

    WhatsApp is finally adding support for travel eSIMs directly in the app, which is welcome news for those filled with wanderlust. These digital data-only eSIM cards help keep people connected while traveling, all while avoiding exorbitant roaming fees.

    Sources indicate that we don't have too much information as to how this all will work just yet, but we do know that the service will be available for purchase via the official app. That'll save a few clicks, as the platform says the buying process has been designed to be "as effortless as sending a message.".

    It's likely this will be a subscription service that folks buy for the duration of a trip, which is how eSIMs offered by other platforms tend to work. WhatsApp claims that people won't have to change their number or anything like that, so it should be a seamless transition.

    WhatsApp just killed the entire eSim industry pic.twitter.com/v2RwgO6Yuj.

    — nilay (@3bitlemon) November 26, 2026.

    "That way, when you land, you can keep using WhatsApp on your same phone number as you normally would without having to find the closest airport kiosk to buy a local SIM card, hunt for a cafe with Wi-FI or rack up roaming charges," the organization wrote in a short blog post.

    According to recent reports, whatsApp has teamed up with a variety of telecom entities to make this possible, including Verizon and Jio. The service is rolling out "in select countries soon." Engadget has reached out to the platform to ask for more details and will upgrade this post when we hear back.

    we did it, you can now schedule messages on WhatsApp.

    — WhatsApp (@WhatsApp) November 25, 2026.

    It has been revealed that this is just the latest feature that has been added to the world's most popular messaging app. The platform recently introduced stickers with sound, to spice up chats, and the ability to schedule messages ahead of time. Group chats can also now hold up to 1,500 people, which is a whole lot of chaos.

    #150392. Breaking: Volvo's big batteries: We drive its updated 2028 plug-in hybrids

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1527 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Volvo's big batteries: We drive its updated 2028 plug-in hybrids

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015, both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric.
    • Recent findings suggest that so instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh.
    • Recent findings suggest that instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015, both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric. As we know, the future hasn’t turned out quite like that, especially in the critically notable US market. At the same time, Europe and China are electrifying, which seems like an argument against spending resources on developing all-latest replacements for models that might not have an eight-year lifespan in most markets.

    Recent findings suggest that so instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh. The exterior styling tweaks are minimal; the bigger three-row XC90 had already been given a fresh look last year, and the XC60 now gains a similar grille and the same matrix headlights, for instance. And that’s no bad thing—both were, and remain, handsome shapes that are popular with Volvo’s customer base.

    Recent findings suggest that instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards. Which means a much bigger battery for the PHEVs, with sufficient capacity for a couple of days of daily driving for most of us before needing to be recharged. There’s also fresh, modern infotainment and interiors that are now even nicer to spend time in than before.

    We first saw the revamped 2028 XC60 (and learned about its technical details and those of the XC90) in September, but with the cars going into production now and due to reach the first US customers in the first quarter of next year, we got the opportunity to spend some seat time with the updated cars.

    Both the midsize XC60 and three-row XC90 use the same PHEV powertrain. Under the hood, there’s a 2.0 L four-cylinder direct-injection gasoline engine that generates 247 hp (184 kW) and 226 lb-ft (306 Nm) together with a 70 hp (50 kW), 122 ft-lb (165 Nm) electric motor, both of which drive the front wheels. At the rear axle there’s a second electric motor, with an output of 174 hp (130 kW) and 228 lb-ft (309 Nm). Combined output for the hybrid system is 455 hp (339 kW) and 560 lb-ft (759 Nm).

    There’s also a much bigger battery, with a net capacity of 37.9 kWh (41.2 kWh gross). If you set the car’s mode to Pure, which relies solely on the rear electric motor for propulsion, that translates to an EPA range estimate of 78 miles (126 km) for the XC60 and 73 miles (116 km) for the larger, draggier XC90. Which is significant—when the average driver drives fewer than 30 miles a day, it means these PHEVs carry enough electrons for a couple of days of tailpipe-emissions-free driving before it needs to be plugged in again or the engine to fire up.

    According to recent reports, when it is time to plug it back in, expect it to take about four hours with a level 2 charger of at least 16 A, or 27 hours if you’re limited to 120 V. In Hybrid mode, where you get the benefit of both electric motors and the gas engine, Volvo expects a combined efficiency of 67 mpge in the XC60, and 61 mpge for the XC90.

    Even if the gas engine is running and you’re in Hybrid or Power mode (which keeps the engine on all the time), you can drive these Volvos as if they were EVs with one-pedal driving: just move the transmission from D to B. The Volvos are always using their electric motors to slow the car before the friction brakes intervene, and in B you get the same amount of lift-off regen regardless of mode. For city traffic, it’s very effective. (In Pure, although only the rear motor deploys energy, both front and rear motors regen brake.).

    Sources indicate that in power mode, with all 455 hp unleashed, you can chirp the wheels on a wet day, but these model year 2028 cars are about one large male human heavier than the outgoing model year, both of which were already pretty heavy. So don’t expect performance-car performance. The XC60 is the sweeter to drive on a winding road, but both are entirely at home cruising on a highway or creeping along in a city, which is where cars like these spend the vast majority of their time. There’s more road intrusion into the cabin of the XC60—the larger Volvo rides on air suspension that does a much better job of filtering that out.

    Sources indicate that A first-drive event like this isn’t the best place to get a good read on real-world efficiency. We usually have to share cars with other journalists, and there’s limited time to drive on roads that may not be representative—too sinuous, or not enough traffic, for example. We need to try all the different drive modes and see how cars respond to different inputs. And it’s rare you’ll spend the entire day with one car, finishing at the same point you started.

    According to recent reports, that said, I can’t give you a definite read on range and efficiency for these two plug-ins. But my unscientific estimate is that my drive partner and I, in an XC60, drove about 60 km in a mix of city driving and higher speeds on the way to Malmo in Sweden, which is on the other side of a gigantic bridge, and we used about half the battery pack to do so. (Volvo asked us to put the PHEVs in Hold or Charge mode at 50 percent to leave some state of charge for whoever drove the cars after lunch.).

    According to recent reports, thus, there was little charge left in the XC90 when it was my turn to drive the final stint back into Copenhagen. Since I wasn’t worried about combined efficiency, I ran the car in Charge mode for about 20 min, regenerating the battery from an indicated 10 km to an indicated 21 km, then switched to Pure once we reached the city, with about 16 km to go.

    Volvo already had a reputation for great automotive interiors, and with this refresh, it has pushed things forward a little. There’s a latest wood finish, new textiles, and new backlighting. The resemblance between the two interiors from the front seat is now quite strong, particularly since the test cars Volvo brought to Denmark wore identical color schemes inside.

    Sources indicate that our final 1.6 km to the hotel took more than 30 minutes to negotiate thanks to a reception for very notable people that apparently took place next to the hotel. Most of this jam was on one street, with our destination in sight, but the frustration was in part ameliorated by Volvo’s secret weapon: its seat massage function.

    Lots of other OEMs offer massaging front seats, which inflate and deflate the internal air bladder to massage your shoulders, back, and sometimes butt. But none massage you with quite the firmness of a Volvo seat. And they have the power to distract you from terrible in-car situations, as I discovered when stuck in a V90 Cross Country with Nigel the Cat, whose way of remonstrating with me about his trip to the feline ophthalmologist was to scream at high volume until he ran out of breath, at which point he’d pant for a few minutes, then start again. The seat in that car is the only reason we both made it home safely. And so, in Copenhagen, I set the seat to pulse and did some box breathing.

    According to recent reports, as well as latest interior materials, you’ll also notice a new infotainment screen in both cars. Gone are the old 9-inch displays, replaced by a new 11.2-inch touchscreen that stands a little proud of the dash rather than recessed into it. Just this one upgrade alone really lifts both interiors; the old, small screen was showing its age. Most Ars readers will recoil at the news that Gemini has replaced the previous Google Assistant, but at least the voice-recognition capabilities are improved. Gemini will still struggle with some commands—I asked it to tell me my current efficiency, which it failed at, but it’s rather good at looking stuff up on the Internet while I drive.

    There are also some updated advanced driver-assistance systems, like a warning if cyclists approach your opening door, and an updated 360-degree parking view. But there’s no point-to-point assist like Mercedes is introducing, or a hands-free “level 2+” system like Super Cruise; Volvo’s experience with the EX90 may have left it a little gun-shy.

    It has been revealed that with a battery big enough for daily driving and a more modern interior experience, there’s a lot to like about both the 2029 XC60 and XC90. However, we still don’t know how much they’ll cost when they go on sale in Q1 next year. With twice the battery capacity, it’s reasonable to expect a slight price rise, but without knowing how much, it’s hard to say whether it’s a good deal or not.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tame says her "whole body was prickling with distress" over what Handbury said.

    An Australian former media executive has admitted he said a child sex abuse survivor and prominent advocate "must be looking to be raped again" because of the way she was dressed at an event.

    Grace Tame, 31, was groomed and abused by a teacher and has been honoured as Australian of the Year in 2021 for her advocacy work on child safety.

    In an op-ed for independent media outlet Crikey, Tame said she overheard Matt Handbury speaking to a friend, and was left distressed by the remark and the failure of others who heard it to intervene.

    Handbury, nephew of Rupert Murdoch and a former executive at his firms, has not responded to a BBC request for comment, but in an email to Tame noted he regretted the "highly objectionable" comment as soon as he said it.

    Matt Handbury is the nephew of Rupert Murdoch and a former executive at his firms.

    Tame wrote in the Crikey article that she confronted Handbury - who she hadn't met before - immediately, and again later in the evening to check she had heard him correctly.

    She stated the encounter at the University of Newly introduced South Wales event last week triggered flashbacks to her abuse and left her feeling like she would vomit.

    "My whole body was prickling in distress," she wrote for Crikey.

    "The many men and women who'd seen the confrontation were incredulous, and quick to express their anger at Matt's behaviour... Ironically though, in a room full of seasoned activists, journalists, lawyers and actual whistleblowers, not one person besides me took Matt to task in the heat of the moment.".

    The next day, in an email seen by the BBC, Handbury, 77, apologised for the "attempt at humour in less than poor taste".

    Sources indicate that "I did make reference to your strikingly attractive get-up... I also remarked: 'She must be looking to be raped again.'.

    He thanked her for "calling me out" and "opening my eyes more fully to this flaw in my nature which I will certainly be discussing with my very non-misogynist shrink".

    "But no-one can deny you looked absolutely fabulous last night," he said, before signing off.

    It has been revealed that handbury ran Murdoch Magazines for 13 years after buying the business from his uncle in 1991. He sold it to Seven Network's subsidiary Pacific Publications in 2004.

    Tame stated Handbury's remarks were "especially egregious" because it referenced a "very real, criminally tested traumatic experience, which he knew about" rather than an "imagined harm".

    "It swiftly reawakened deep-seated physical wounds and haunting memories. How is that funny?".

    According to recent reports, from the age of 15, Tame was groomed and raped by her 58-year-old maths teacher Nicolaas Ockert Bester. He was later found guilty and served one year and nine months in jail for sexually abusing Tame when she was his student in 2011.

    "They're not always as extreme, public or evidenced, but these kinds of experiences are part of my everyday life," Tame wrote on Instagram of Handbury's remarks.

    It has been revealed that "I'm tired of the maltreatment; and the gaslighting that follows. Tired of being provoked, then asked why I'm angry.

    "I'm tired of copping more flak for fighting injustice than those who mete it out.".

    If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line.

    Latest Update: The canceled Tesla Cybertruck is the fastest-selling used truck in America

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (579 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tesla Cybertruck sales never reached the lofty heights CEO Elon Musk predicted when it launched.
    • It has been revealed that the automotive search engine and research platform analyzed more than 1.1 million sales of one- to five-year-old used vehicles in October 2026 and measured the average days on market by drivetrain, vehicle type, and individual model.
    • Recent findings suggest that according to iSeeCars.com, the Cybertruck’s sales performance lines up with a broader pattern in the used vehicle market: Used battery electric vehicles are hot sellers right now, with 16 of the 25 fastest-selling used cars fully electric.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tesla Cybertruck sales never reached the lofty heights CEO Elon Musk predicted when it launched. But the futuristic, steel-clad EV is finding new life in the used car market, according to analysis of sales figures by iSeeCars.com.

    It has been revealed that the automotive search engine and research platform analyzed more than 1.1 million sales of one- to five-year-old used vehicles in October 2026 and measured the average days on market by drivetrain, vehicle type, and individual model. The upshot: The Tesla Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used truck, averaging just 39.1 days on the market compared with 65.5 days for trucks overall. Used Cybertrucks sold faster than any other truck, including the Ford Maverick Hybrid, which held the No. 2 spot, and the Rivian R1T, in third place.

    Recent findings suggest that according to iSeeCars.com, the Cybertruck’s sales performance lines up with a broader pattern in the used vehicle market: Used battery electric vehicles are hot sellers right now, with 16 of the 25 fastest-selling used cars fully electric. EVs are even edging out hybrids in terms of average days on market. EVs average 45.6 days on market compared to 54.5 days for hybrids and 61 days for gasoline-powered vehicles. Not every EV is selling well, however. For instance, iSeeCars.com found that the Cadillac Escalade IQ was the slowest-selling vehicle in the study, averaging 134.3 days on the market, more than twice the overall industry average.

    Karl Brauer, executive analyst at iSeeCars.com, told TechCrunch that high gasoline prices have changed consumer-buying habits, prompting more people to opt for an EV or hybrid over an internal combustion engine vehicle. If high prices persist, as they have since March, that trend could continue.

    Keep in mind that these were October sales, the month before Musk revealed Tesla would stop making the Cybertruck in 2027. Fuel prices and the relative rarity of Cybertrucks in the used car market were driving demand even before the cancellation announcement, Brauer said.

    “The Cybertruck has only been out for a few years, so you have a lot of used ones coming off lease and entering the used car market for the first time,” he stated, adding that used Cybertrucks are cheap relative to their MSRP.

    The impending cancellation will likely fuel used Cybertruck sales, although the pace may ebb and flow over the next year.

    Industry observers note that “The canceling of the latest Cybertruck is making people kind of aware — it’s like, oh wow, these things aren’t going to be coming anymore,” Brauer stated. “Whatever demand is for them, supply will not be continuing to grow.”.

    Brauer remarked that once production of the Cybertruck ends — which is expected in summer 2027 — sales of used versions may pop once again.

    “When the last one is being produced, that’ll probably reignite things again, and for a few months after that,” he said.

    According to recent reports, during Black Friday, the Anker 100W Universal Charger is on sale for $59.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, a $20 discount from its list price. That’s a few dollars lower than the previous best, with both the dark gray and silver versions available from all three retailers. With four USB ports and support for over 200 countries, you can keep all of your devices charged wherever you end up.

    Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.

    Recent findings suggest that anker’s travel charger supports outlets in over 200 countries, including Type A for the United States, Canada, Japan, and China; Type C for the European Union; and Type G for the UK and Singapore. It doesn’t support Type I, the outlet used in Australia, New Zealand, and Argentina. Also, there’s no AC adapter. It’s a USB-only affair. To that end, you can charge up to four devices at once, with three USB-C ports and one USB-A port, with two of the USB-C ports capable of delivering up to 100W when used individually. There’s even a tiny display on the unit that lets you check how much power is going to your devices at a glance.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Costco members can get some pretty great deals.

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    If you're looking to buy a Nintendo Switch 2, Costco is one of a handful of retailers offering $50 off the console. And for those willing to spend a bit more than the $499 Amazon and Best Buy are selling the Mario Kart World bundle for, Costco's exclusive $520 package is a better value.

    According to recent reports, that's because you get 12 months of Nintendo Switch Online included with your purchase, instead of the three months that normally comes with the Mario Kart Bundle. That subscription also comes with Nintendo's Expansion Pack, which allows you to play Nintendo 64, Game Boy Advance and Game Cube games on your fresh console. Normally, a 12 Nintendo Switch Online subscription with Expansion Pack costs $50, and the Mario Kart World bundle costs $550 when it's not on sale. So you're saving about $80 compared to buying those two items separately at their regular price. Just note you'll need a Costco membership to take advantage of the deal.

    Engadget senior reporter Sam Rutherford gave the Nintendo Switch 2 a score of 93 when he reviewed it in 2025. If you already own the original Switch, its successor is a no-brainer, offering a larger screen, far better performance and more durable Joy-Con controllers. What's more, the Switch 2 library has only grown since launch, with a great mix of exclusives like The Ocarina of Time and Pokémon Pokopia, alongside plenty of ports and indies, available on the console.

    Costco is one of the better retailers to buy the AirPods Pro 3 or AirPods 5 from this Black Friday. Not only has the tech giant discounted both pairs of earbuds, but it's also throwing in AppleCare+. The AirPods Pro 3 are $69 off their regular $249 price, and come with two years of Apple's extended warranty coverage, while the AirPods 5 with wireless charging case are $130, down from $149, and include one-year of extended Apple support. With the AirPods Pro 3, a year of AppleCare+ costs $2 per month or $20 annually. For the AirPods 5, the price is $1.49 per month or $15 annually, Either way you're not only saving money by going with Costco, you're also getting a bit of peace of mind with extra coverage.

    According to recent reports, you can get the AirPods Pro 3 from Amazon and Best Buy for less money overall ($149 versus $179), but neither manufacturer is including complimentary AppleCare+ coverage like Costco. If you were planning to extend the warranty for your new earbuds anyway, Costco has the best offer.

    Sources indicate that engadget reviewed both the AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods 5, giving them scores of 90 and 88, respectively. With active noise cancellation now standard across Apple's current AirPods line, you can't really go wrong with either model. One thing to note is there are two different versions of the AirPods 5. The variant Costco has discounted is the one you want to buy if you decide to go with the AirPods 5. It comes with a wireless charging case that offers volume gesture controls and audible Find My features.

    It has been revealed that like many other US retailers, Costco has discounted the Oura Ring 5 by $100, bringing the wearable down to $299 and its lowest price yet. All three color options — silver, black and gold — are $100 off, and inclusive of the retailer's exclusive bundle, which adds an extra year of warranty and a second USB-C charging station. Like the Switch 2 bundle, this deal is only available to Costco members.

    Sources indicate that the Oura Ring 5 is another Engadget favorite. Senior Editor Daniel Cooper reviewed it earlier this year and a give it a glowing 9 out 10. The fact the Oura Ring 5 is 40 percent smaller than its predecessor, while offering an even better seven days of battery life, make it an easy recommendation for anyone looking to try a smart ring for the first time.

    Look at you considering a Sonos Arc Ultra. The tech giant's flagship soundbar is $250 off for Black Friday, making it right now $850 instead of its usual eye-watering price of $1100. That price also beats the $900 the Arc Ultra was briefly listed for last month. If you decide to buy a Sonos Sub at the same time, Costco will take an extra $70 off your total transaction. You're still paying $1,500 before tax for both devices, but I imagine there won't be many opportunities to buy a complete Arc Ultra setup for less.

    Industry observers note that engadget's resident audio guru Billy Steele gave the Arc Ultra a score of 87 back in 2024. The soundbar marked the debut of Sonos' Sound Motion technology, which the organization claimed would improve the Arc's bass performance. In Steele's testing, the soundbar did offer better low-frequency performance, as well as clarity and depth, than its predecessor. The Arc is pricey, but if you don't want to deal with a multi-speaker setup, and all the wires that come with one, the Sonos Arc Ultra at $850 is one of the best high-end soundbars you can buy. And even if you're not a CostCo member, Sonos' own Black Friday sale has the Arc Ultra available for the same $850 price, along with a bunch of other solid discounts on the company's speakers and headphones.

    Sources indicate that this past summer, my home of Toronto had a few days of terrible air quality due to the forest fires that ravaged northern Ontario. I was thankful then that the year before I had bought a Levoit air purifier. Even when air quality is fine, an air purifier can make your home more comfortable. Costco has discounted one of the best models you can buy, the Dyson HushJet, by $150 to $199. That's an all-time low price for the Dyson device, and the best price you'll find for it during Black Friday, beating even Amazon by about $50.

    In a recent development, engadget included the HushJet in our roundup of the best air purifiers you can buy. Its aesthetic might not be for everyone, but true to its name, the HushJet is among the quietest purifiers our reviewer tested, and it does a great job of forcefully circulating air.
